title: Indian Accent Named India's Top Standalone Restaurant for Fourth Straight Year
excerpt: At the Hospitality Horizon Top 50 Restaurant Awards 2026, the New Delhi flagship kept its No. 1 standalone ranking — and parent group EHV International placed seven restaurants in the top 20.
body:
• Indian Accent, New Delhi has been named India's No. 1 standalone restaurant for the fourth consecutive year at the Hospitality Horizon Top 50 Restaurant Awards 2026, PTI reported.
  • Its parent, EHV International, took seven of the top 20 places: Indian Accent Mumbai at No. 5, Comorin Gurugram at No. 8, Hosa Goa at No. 12, Comorin Mumbai at No. 14, Chor Bizarre Delhi at No. 17 and Fireback Mumbai at No. 19.
  • The awards, split between hotel and standalone restaurants, were decided by a 78-member industry jury and presented at a ceremony at the Four Seasons Hotel in Mumbai.
  • Planning a special-occasion meal in Delhi or Mumbai? The Delhi original — on Asia's 50 Best Restaurants list for 13 consecutive years — remains the group's flagship booking.

Indian Accent has done it again. The New Delhi restaurant, known for its modern Indian cuisine, has retained the No. 1 position among India's standalone restaurants for the fourth consecutive year at the Hospitality Horizon Top 50 Restaurant Awards 2026, according to PTI.

The honour was received at the Mumbai ceremony by Indian Accent's executive chef Shantanu Mehrotra, EHV International chief operating officer Nitin Mathur and the group's founder chairman Rohit Khattar. The awards recognise restaurants in two categories — restaurants in hotels and standalone restaurants — and were decided by a jury of 78 members from the food and hospitality industry, Hospitality Horizon publisher Shafquat Ali said at the ceremony, held at the Four Seasons Hotel in Mumbai.

"I would like to congratulate EHV International for sweeping so many awards, including Indian Accent remaining at No. 1 for the 4th year in a row."

— Shafquat Ali, Publisher, Hospitality Horizon

One group, seven of the top 20

The wider story of the night was the depth of the group behind Indian Accent. EHV International secured seven positions in the top 20. Indian Accent's Mumbai outlet placed fifth, and Comorin in Gurugram — the group's restaurant built around regional Indian flavours — took eighth, giving EHV three restaurants in the top 10. Further down the list, Hosa in Goa, which specialises in South Indian cuisine, placed 12th; Comorin's Mumbai outlet was 14th; Chor Bizarre in Delhi, known for its Indian dining experience, was 17th; and Fireback in Mumbai, the group's Thai restaurant, was 19th.

"These are the most credible and the ultimate Restaurant Awards in the country," Ali said. "I am grateful to our sponsors but most of all, to the industry for taking out the time to attend and to our incredible jury who allow us to keep these awards so unimpeachable."

A flagship with a long record

The Hospitality Horizon result adds to a long run of recognition for the Delhi restaurant, which has featured on the Asia's 50 Best Restaurants list for 13 consecutive years. The brand's Mumbai outpost, which opened in 2023 at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre, has been building its own record: in July 2026 it entered 50 Best Discovery, the curated guide compiled from votes by the 50 Best academies, as Indian Television Dot Com reported.

For readers planning a meal around the list: the Delhi original is the flagship and the four-time No. 1; the Mumbai restaurant at the NMACC is the same kitchen's newer room, ranked fifth among standalones this year; and Comorin's two outlets offer the group's more relaxed, regional-Indian format in Gurugram and Mumbai. Four years at the top of one list is a streak few Indian restaurants have matched — and on this year's evidence, the group behind it is widening the lead rather than defending it.
nri_angle: For diaspora readers visiting India, the list doubles as a booking guide: Indian Accent in Delhi and Mumbai, plus EHV's Comorin, Hosa, Chor Bizarre and Fireback, all placed in the national top 20.
